session.title: Rights, Representation and the Assembly's Authority

primarySource.publisher: Parliament Digital Library, Lok Sabha Secretariat

speakers.name: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
speakers.positionSummary: Fixes the programme of business, regulates interruptions and speaking time, resolves document-text questions and adjourns the House.

speakers.name: Several Members
speakers.positionSummary: Respond collectively to the Chair's proposal for completing business before Christmas.

speakers.name: Frank Anthony
speakers.positionSummary: Offers longer working hours and Sunday sittings but strongly resists reconvening during the Christmas-to-New-Year period.

speakers.name: Jawaharlal Nehru
speakers.positionSummary: Notes that the United Nations General Assembly had sat on Sundays to expedite work.

speakers.name: Kiron Sankar Roy
speakers.positionSummary: Warns against rushing the Assembly Rules and asks that members receive them days before general discussion.

speakers.name: B. G. Kher
speakers.positionSummary: Urges long sittings and a time limit on rule amendments so the preliminary business can be completed before Christmas.

speakers.name: Syama Prasad Mookerjee
speakers.positionSummary: Opposes meeting during Christmas week and insists that the Rules need reasonable circulation and study time.

speakers.name: Somnath Lahiri
speakers.positionSummary: Argues that the Assembly remains constrained by British power, calls for a more explicit break with imperialism and presses self-determination, representation and concrete rights.

speakers.name: Rajkrushna Bose
speakers.positionSummary: Interrupts Lahiri to ask whether he supports or opposes the Resolution.

speakers.name: Vishwambhar Dayal Tripathi
speakers.positionSummary: Also presses Lahiri to clarify whether he supports the Resolution or Jayakar's amendment.

speakers.name: Unnamed Member
speakers.positionSummary: Asks Lahiri what concrete electoral arrangement he proposes.

speakers.name: H. V. Kamath
speakers.positionSummary: Questions whether Lahiri is reintroducing an argument previously ruled out of order.

speakers.name: Hansa Mehta
speakers.positionSummary: Supports the Resolution and focuses on equality of status and opportunity for women without separate electorates or reserved privileges.

speakers.name: P. R. Thakur
speakers.positionSummary: Supports the Resolution while demanding adequate political safeguards and representation for the Depressed Classes.

speakers.name: Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar
speakers.positionSummary: Rejects Jayakar's competence objections, defends an objectives declaration at the outset and treats the Cabinet Mission statement as machinery rather than a complete constitutional statute.

speakers.name: Jaipal Singh
speakers.stance: Supports Resolution · demands equal place for Adivasis
speakers.positionSummary: Supports the Resolution while foregrounding Adivasi exclusion, democratic traditions, representation and equal opportunity.

speakers.name: Suresh Chandra Banerjee
speakers.positionSummary: Questions the correct wording in competing printed versions of the Cabinet Mission statement.

speakers.name: Debi Prasad Khaitan
speakers.positionSummary: Argues from a practical institutional perspective that the Assembly must define objectives, central subjects and minority machinery rather than remain paralysed by gaps in the Cabinet Mission statement.

speakers.name: Damber Singh Gurung
speakers.positionSummary: Supports proceeding while demanding recognition and representation for Indian Gurkhas as a minority community.

speakers.name: Hari Singh Gour
speakers.positionSummary: Rejects treating the Assembly as a creature of the Cabinet Mission and argues that its responsibility runs directly to the people of India.

speakers.name: Dakshayani Velayudhan
speakers.positionSummary: Links the Republic to social emancipation, rejects caste-based separatism and argues that Harijans must gain equality as Indians through an independent social order.

interventions.summary: The Chair lists unfinished work: the Objectives Resolution, Assembly Rules, the disputed interpretation/Federal Court question and election of committees. He proposes intensive sittings to finish before Christmas if possible.
Several members indicate support for the Chair's proposal to work intensively and finish before Christmas.
Frank Anthony says Christian members can work long hours and even Sunday, but asks the Assembly not to reconvene between Christmas and New Year.
Nehru notes that the United Nations General Assembly had sat on Sundays to expedite its work.
Kiron Sankar Roy argues that members should receive the Rules several days before debate and warns against assuming they can be passed in only two or three days.
B. G. Kher proposes long sittings and a firm cut-off for amendments so the Rules and other business can be completed before Christmas.
Syama Prasad Mookerjee opposes meeting during Christmas week and says the Rules must be circulated with enough time for study and amendments.
The Chair says the Assembly will attempt to finish by Monday, explains the Rules Committee's consensus-seeking work and then returns the House to the Objectives Resolution.

Somnath Lahiri argues that the constitutional process still operates under British military and political power and calls for a more direct break with imperial control rather than relying on the Cabinet Mission framework.
Rajkrushna Bose challenges Lahiri to make clear whether he is supporting or opposing the Resolution.
The Chair asks the House to let Lahiri continue but reminds him of relevance and the time limit, balancing the speaker's right to present an independent view with the mood of the House.
Vishwambhar Dayal Tripathi again asks whether Lahiri supports the Resolution or the amendment.
Lahiri argues that unity cannot rest on compulsion, presses a stronger conception of self-determination and criticises rights language that lacks concrete institutional guarantees.
An unnamed member asks Lahiri what arrangement he proposes in place of communal representation.
Lahiri proposes proportional representation with adult suffrage and joint electorates as a way to secure representation while reducing religious political separation.
H. V. Kamath questions whether Lahiri is reviving material connected to an amendment that had already been ruled out of order.

Hansa Mehta supports the Resolution and argues that women need equality of status and opportunity, social, economic and political justice, and full human rights rather than special privileges or separate electorates.
interventions.excerpt: equality of status but equality of opportunity

interventions.summary: P. R. Thakur supports the Resolution but argues that the Depressed Classes require adequate safeguards, political representation and serious consideration as the Assembly designs minority protections.
The Chair calls Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar and permits him to speak seated; members voice no objection.

Alladi rejects Jayakar's objections, arguing that the Cabinet Mission statement provides machinery rather than an exhaustive statute and that a constituent body must state its directing objective at the outset.
interventions.excerpt: a constitution can be settled by Indians for Indians

interventions.summary: Jaipal Singh supports the Resolution on behalf of Adivasis while attacking their historic exclusion, insisting on equal treatment, representation and recognition of tribal democratic traditions.
interventions.excerpt: You cannot teach democracy to the tribal people

interventions.summary: The Chair responds to questions about conflicting printed versions of the Cabinet Mission statement and promises to investigate the textual discrepancy.
Suresh Chandra Banerjee asks whether the correct word in the Cabinet Mission statement is 'due' or 'full' and points out that members' copies differ.

Debi Prasad Khaitan supports the Resolution and argues that the Assembly must define objectives, central subjects and minority machinery rather than allow omissions in the Cabinet Mission statement to paralyse constitution-making.
Damber Singh Gurung supports the Resolution but demands minority recognition and adequate representation for Indian Gurkhas, including in the future Advisory Committee.

Hari Singh Gour argues that the Constituent Assembly is responsible to the people of India rather than being a subordinate creature of the Cabinet Mission, rejects indefinite deference to absent parties and discusses the constitutional position of the States.
interventions.excerpt: the Constituent Assembly is the voice of the people of India

interventions.summary: Dakshayani Velayudhan supports the Resolution as a framework for a free social order, rejects caste-based separatism and external paternalism, and insists that the emancipation of Harijans lies in equality within an independent India.
interventions.excerpt: a Constituent Assembly not only frames a constitution, but also gives the people a new framework of life

interventions.summary: At 1:15 PM the Chair adjourns the Assembly until 11:00 AM on Saturday, 21 December 1946.
